title: W9 counts streaming spawns over the whole run (ticks 1..=3000) while its target and per-host bound are window-scoped, diluting the pinned ×0.95 window contract
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:418 `MIN_LAND := EXPECTED * 95 / 100`; :426 `for tick in u64(1)..=SURGE_END {`; :438 `stream_spawned += 1` (inside that loop, counting class-1 spawns from tick 1, not from SURGE_START 1200); :466 `bound := ceil_cap + accrue * WINDOW / 1000` compared against `per_host_spawns[...]`, which is also accumulated since tick 1. The failure message itself says "streaming window spawns".
detail: Card W9 pins the surge WINDOW's count ≥ expected×0.95. ~1200 pre-window base spawns count toward MIN_LAND, so the test passes while the in-window count is as low as ~88% of expected; conversely the window-sized per-host bound is applied to a full-run count.
recommended_fix: Gate both counters on `tick >= SURGE_START` (count window spawns and per-host window spawns only). Test-file-only change; no golden or core churn.

title: Two stale 120-tick growth references survive the GROWTH_INTERVAL_TICKS 120→40 re-tune
evidence: demos/growth.dem:7 `# (GROWTH_INTERVAL_TICKS = 120 @ 20 Hz), deterministically from the seed + the` (directly under line 5's `# GROWTH_INTERVAL_TICKS 120 -> 40 so the capped era-3 demand can LAND as an`); core/node_health_test.odin:286 `step_n(&s, 400, cat) // 3 growth windows (120 ticks each) + margin` (400 ticks is now 10 windows of 40).
detail: The re-tune updated growth.odin and other comments but missed these two; a future re-bless reader tracing the growth timeline gets contradictory interval numbers in the doc surfaces.
recommended_fix: Update growth.dem:7 to `= 40 @ 20 Hz` and the node_health_test comment to `10 growth windows (40 ticks each)`.

title: W10 block comment names the sink as "(id 3)" but the sink is node id 2
evidence: core/demand_test.odin:495 `// TWO residentials: the sourcing one (id 0, at its cap) + the sink (id 3)` vs :502 `r2 := topology_spawn_node(&s.topology, res_idx, {32, 15}, cat) // the sink (id 2)` — the fixture spawns r0=0, router=1, r2=2 (topology_spawn_node assigns sequential ids from next_node_id).
detail: The block comment is stale from an earlier fixture shape; the inline comment on the same spawn is correct. Misleading for anyone reasoning about the dst-exclusion set.
recommended_fix: Correct the block comment to "the sink (id 2)".

title: §1b breaks the file's temp-scratch delete discipline: the eligible-set arrays are never deleted and the sink-side slots array is discarded unnamed
evidence: core/flow.odin:737 `sink_ids, sink_w, _ := collect_terminals(&state.topology, cat, spec.sink_role)`; :739-741 `e_ids := make([dynamic]u32, 0, len(src_ids), context.temp_allocator)` (+e_w, e_slots); :773-774 `delete(src_ids); delete(src_w); delete(src_slots)` / `delete(sink_ids); delete(sink_w)` — no delete for e_ids/e_w/e_slots. collect_terminals' doc (flow.odin:576): `Scratch-allocated; the caller frees all three arrays.`
detail: The surrounding code deletes every temp scratch (src/sink arrays; drops/forwarded via defer delete). The discarded sink slots array cannot be freed by the caller, violating the proc's own doc contract; per-tick free_all masks it.
recommended_fix: Delete e_ids/e_w/e_slots after the spec's pick loop; capture the sink slots in a named var and delete it (or split collect_terminals so sinks don't allocate slots).
